content.comment_body: Hello! I recently tested the math capabilities in [product_name] and managed to create an accurate user-defined function (UDF) for the sine function. The math function block can achieve impressive results; it calculates the sine for any integer value and multiplies the outcome by 1000 ('msine' - milli sine). The results are quite precise, with a rounding error theoretically at +/- 0.5, but I observed +/- 0.6. There were 34 function blocks involved. Although I don’t need such precision at the moment, this could serve as a strong exercise for students studying PLCs and trigonometry. It's possible to generate true sine oscillations (as opposed to approximated triangular signals) using only 10 function blocks including a PI controller, as shown in the attached image. Summing two sine waves with different frequencies and amplitudes can simulate 'realistic' signal data for demonstrations or software testing.
That image with the sine curve is visually appealing, but posting just the UDF itself would benefit fellow members more. Regards, [user_name]
OK! The attachment contains the complete sine UDF test program.
I think [user_name] meant sharing the actual UDF, not just a program that uses the UDF.
Is there any protected way to publish UDFs? If not, I'll share it regardless. I’d appreciate feedback on my solution. I've also created programs using the same UDF for cosine and tangent functions.
Next time, if you bring up a problem, I'll provide a program that includes the solution as a UDF.
Hello, are you saying my comments weren’t quite appropriate for the forum? My apologies; I just wanted to celebrate my progress in [product_name] programming.

Hello again! I tested on a different computer and found the UDF can be extracted from the shared example and reused elsewhere. You can even extend it by entering a password ('logom'). The UDF will display with a red question mark. I’ve now included the UDF in the attachment. Note: This UDF contains additional UDFs inside, and I’m not certain which version it currently is.

analysis.insight_summary: Users developed an accurate sine function using [product_name] platforms, demonstrating advanced use of math function blocks for trigonometric calculations such as sine, cosine, and tangent. While the solution requires many function blocks for precision, only minor rounding errors were reported. There is interest in sharing and reusing user-defined functions, with questions about secure distribution and best practices. The community is keen on exchanging technical solutions, although some users showed uncertainty about the optimal way to share UDFs.
